question.text: Compound A, <math><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>8</mn></mrow></msub><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">H</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>9</mn></mrow></msub><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">r</mi></math> , gives a white precipitate when warmed with alcoholic <math><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub></math> . Oxidation of A gives an acid B, <math><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>8</mn></mrow></msub><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">H</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>6</mn></mrow></msub><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>4</mn></mrow></msub><mo>.</mo></math> B easily forms anhydride on heating. Identity the compound A.
